# Lemuri

> Lemuri is a free, open source (MIT) desktop SSH console for the servers and VPS you manage: a tree of hosts, tabs and split terminals, uploads and downloads over SFTP from the terminal, live metrics, an encrypted password vault, one-file backups and end-to-end encrypted sharing of hosts with a team. It is written in Java with JavaFX and runs on Linux (developed and tested on Ubuntu with GNOME); macOS builds from source but is not tested on a real Mac yet.

There are no ready-made packages yet: Lemuri builds and runs from source with JDK 21 and `unzip` installed:

```
git clone https://github.com/getlemuri/lemuri
cd lemuri
./mvnw javafx:run
```

Maven is not needed: the wrapper downloads it the first time.

## Main features

- Host tree: nested folders you drag around, a mark showing which servers answer on their SSH port, a badge with the open sessions. Double-click opens the shell.
- Tabs and split panes: one tab per session, split a terminal side by side or one above the other, on the same host or another; sync sends what you type to every pane.
- Files: drag files or folders onto a terminal to upload them to the shell's current folder; after `ls`, right-click a name to download it. Overwrites are shown before anything moves; files are written under a temporary name until complete; symbolic links are not followed.
- Live metrics: CPU, memory, disks, uptime, pending updates (and how many are security fixes) and whether a reboot is required, read over SSH with no agent on the server.
- Ghost mode: the window becomes a see-through terminal on the desktop, anchored to a screen edge; F11 hides and shows it.
- Backup: one encrypted file with hosts, vault and selected SSH keys; importing never overwrites `~/.ssh`.
- Import of `~/.ssh/config`, `ProxyJump` and keys included.
- Jump hosts like `ssh -J`; every host key at every hop is checked against `known_hosts`, new ones confirmed by hand.
- Clickable terminal: after `ls`, double-click a folder to enter it or a text file to open it in `nano`.
- Encrypted vault: passwords encrypted with AES-GCM under a key derived from the master password with Argon2id; key passphrases are never saved.
- Local shell tab next to the servers, and a command line launcher: `lemuri -s db-01` opens a host's shell in the current terminal.
- Team sharing: send a host with its credentials to a teammate, sealed for them and signed by you, with no server or account. Keys are exchanged once (fingerprint compared by voice, or a 6-digit code on the same network). On a local network hosts go directly between PCs (UDP 47820 for discovery on private addresses, TCP 47821); otherwise as an encrypted text sent by email or chat.
